objective: Start a complete batch of promise-returning workers, wait before the next batch, and preserve snapshotted order and original failures.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Promise.all and bounded concurrency remain current application tools.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Batching uploads or independent requests avoids uncontrolled parallel starts.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Snapshot membership, ordering and failure boundaries transfer to queue-like workflows.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The exercise combines async/await, slice and aggregation after their foundations.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: A live input can add/change work mid-run; waiting on a hung peer can hide a rejection.

defects: Reference/junior reread mutable input membership after awaits while senior pre-cut batches.
Size bounds, worker argument count and exact opaque values/reasons were unstated.
An implementation reading live input passed every previous check.
The first pre-release mutation fixture assumed the first worker had already registered when inBatches returned, falsely rejecting a valid initial-await implementation.
rationale: Snapshot items before any worker and make all boards use that captured membership; keep slice plus whole-batch Promise.all. Bound dense/frozen arrays to 1000 and size to positive integers through 1000. Workers always return ordinary native Promises and do not throw synchronously, matching the taught domain; no synchronous-throw batch guarantee is invented. Require exactly one item argument, all batch starts before await, fresh dense output and exact reasons/values. A rejected current worker settles the result even beside a never-settling peer, stops later batches and does not cancel producers already started. Explain total linear wrapper/snapshot/result work excluding workers/wait. Cases mutate later items after the first batch starts, reject beside a never-settling peer, inspect original opaque values/arity and exercise one batch of 1000 with observed concurrency 1000. Revision 2 creates the producer gate before invoking the wrapper. This preserves the membership-mutation check without requiring synchronous first-batch startup. A new valid async variant captures items and awaits Promise.resolve before starting its first batch; both real Submit and isolated Run accept it. No timing requirement is added to the task.

objective: Suppress superseded search outcomes using per-wrapper call identity, including rejection and synchronous reentry.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Closures and async outcome ordering remain standard JavaScript patterns.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Search interfaces need to ignore obsolete results.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Logical call identity transfers to other overlapping asynchronous work.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The bounded wrapper builds on counters, closures and await.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: An older successful answer or error must not overwrite a newer interaction.

defects: Senior let a synchronous search throw escape before returning a Promise.
Literal producer-settlement wording disagreed with the await-continuation behavior of the implementations for already fulfilled promises.
Opaque argument/value/reason identity, stale shape, reentry and per-run cost scope were unstated.
rationale: Align senior to async try/await and register the call before invoking search. Clarify that freshness is decided when the wrapper handles its outcome, so back-to-back calls over already fulfilled promises still stale the first; completed outcomes never change retroactively. Define up to 20 unchanged opaque arguments, at most 10000 calls per independent wrapper, a nonthenable/native-Promise or synchronously throwing search without this dependence, exact values/reasons and stale-only object shape. Author linear per-run argument/handler work, constant factory setup and exclusion of search/wait. Core #410 keeps the inspector unknown/25 XP rather than presenting factory construction as this per-run target. Cases cover immediate fulfilled races, returned rejection for sync throw, reentrant newer start before old throw, opaque args/values/reasons and 1000 overlapping calls with only the final outcome fresh.

objective: Clone a serializable graph with an ancestor Set, replacing only back-edges while expanding repeated shared subtrees normally.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: JSON serialization and cyclic object graphs remain current JavaScript concerns.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Logging or transporting data with parent links needs a defined cycle policy.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Ancestor-path tracking versus a global seen set is a reusable graph distinction.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The task combines recursion, plain records/arrays and Set after their foundations.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Prototype-like keys can disappear and shared data can be falsely marked circular.

defects: Junior used an ancestor array and unsafe ordinary-object assignment for literal __proto__ keys.
Senior used a replacer/ancestor-array strategy instead of the expressly requested copy and Set approach.
Plain-data scope, key ordering, sparse arrays, special Number/Unicode values and expanded-output input size were unstated.
The unsafe junior passed the prior checks.
rationale: Retain the correct reference and align junior/senior to copied arrays/own-key records with an ancestor Set; junior uses a null prototype and senior safe fromEntries. Define own enumerable string keys, ordinary sparse arrays, ignored named/nonenumerable/Symbol keys, standard primitive JSON behavior and no hooks/getters/proxies/BigInt. Frozen cycles/shared objects remain unchanged. Bound expanded occurrence/depth/text size, and author linear work/space in expanded traversal plus inspected key/string units, counting repeated shared subtrees each time. Average constant-time Set and linear enumeration/serialization are stated model assumptions, not language guarantees. Cases include a frozen null-prototype own __proto__ cycle, sparse self-array, shared self-cycles per sibling, depth-100 back-link, 1000 repeated shared records, nonfinite/-0/Unicode/lone-surrogate primitives and numeric/toJSON/nonenumerable/Symbol key behavior.

objective: Retry sequentially within an exact budget, return the first success and forward the final original failure without accumulating recursion.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Async loops and error propagation remain core JavaScript techniques.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: A bounded retry loop is a practical control-flow building block.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Exact budgets and sequential completion transfer to other repeated attempts.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The exercise teaches looping over promise failures without external network dependencies.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Extra calls, overlapping work or the wrong failure reason change the operation performed.

defects: Senior recursively retried despite the authored loop approach and called fn once with a zero budget.
Zero-budget behavior, argument arity, exact values/reasons and sequential pending behavior were unspecified.
The generic skeleton did not guide the loop/last-reason mechanism.
rationale: Keep the correct loop-based reference/junior and replace senior with a loop. Define attempts 0..1000, zero as no call and rejection with undefined because no last error exists (matching existing reference/junior), a zero-argument native-Promise or synchronously throwing fn, no overlap/extra call and exact opaque values/reasons. Replace the generic skeleton with loop/try/lastError guidance. Author worst-case linear wrapper time in 1+budget and constant retained wrapper state, excluding fn/wait. Cases cover zero budget, final Symbol reason after varied failures, synchronous throw followed by exact opaque success, zero-argument/count checks, 1000 sequential rejections with maximum active count one and no new call while an attempt remains pending.
